Seatrium wins another FPSO integration contract from Modec for deployment in Guyana
article:
Seatrium has won a contract from MODEC, a regular customer, to build the Essequibo 1899 Floating Production, Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel.

The value of the contract is not disclosed.

This FPSO, which will be deployed in offshore Guyana, will be Seatrium’s second FPSO integration project for Tokyo-listed MODEC in offshore Guyana.

The FPSO is designed with an initial production capacity of approximately 150,000 barrels of oil per day (BOPD), together with associated gas and water handling capabilities, and will be moored at a water depth of approximately 1,025 metres.

The award follows Seatrium’s successful completion of topside installation and integration for FPSO Errea Wittu, which recently arrived in Guyana for deployment at the Uaru development.

Under the contract awarded, Seatrium will undertake topside module integration works, fabrication of the flare tower and crane pedestal, and provide support for pre-commissioning and commissioning activities.

“This award reinforces Seatrium’s position as the preferred integration partner for complex FPSO projects,” says Marlin Khiew, executive vice president of Seatrium Energy (Projects) & President, LATAM.

“Our continued role across every FPSO integration project awarded for Guyana Projects to date reflects the confidence customers place in our execution capabilities.

“Leveraging experience and operational insights gained from successive projects, we continue to enhance execution certainty and efficiency for MODEC,” he adds.

Seatrium shares closed at $1.76 on Nov 16, down 2.22%.

title: Wheat falls on optimism about Black Sea talks, Argentine supply
article:
(Nov 16): Wheat futures in Chicago fell on optimism about progress in negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict in the Black Sea and expectations of strong supplies from the Southern Hemisphere.

The most-active contract fell as much as 1.1%, though it later pared some of those losses. Hard red winter wheat also fell. US President Donald Trump is expected to meet with his Chinese and Russian counterparts later this week, with the escalation of tensions in the Black Sea expected to be discussed.

Persistent disruptions to shipping in the Black Sea have curbed wheat outflows from the key producing region, threatening supplies across Asia and Africa. Still, optimism about a resolution is tempered by continued attacks by both Russia and Ukraine.

“Russia-Ukraine fighting continues despite renewed peace negotiations,” said Joe Davis, a director of commodity sales at Futures International LLC. “This is keeping Black Sea shipping risks elevated.”

At the same time, the forecast for Argentina’s wheat crop was raised last week to 24.3 million tonnes, up from a previous estimate of 23.8 million tonnes.

Wheat prices are factoring in both the disruption to Black Sea export flows and abundant Southern Hemisphere supplies, CM Navigator analysts wrote in a note.

See also: Copper sinks to four-month low on tech rout, China growth woes
• Wheat fell 0.5% to US$6.04 a bushel at 6.31am in Chicago
